seo.description: What interiors really cost on Dwarka Expressway in 2026: per sq ft rates and full-home budgets for mid-segment, premium and luxury societies, line by line.

title: Interior Design Cost for Dwarka Expressway Apartments: 2026 Benchmarks by Builder Tier
author: Shivam Kumar

featuredImage.alt: Living room interior in a Sobha apartment, Sector 108 Gurgaon, designed by The Omega Group

excerpt: A mid-segment 3BHK and a branded 4BHK are both "Dwarka Expressway apartments," but their interior budgets have almost nothing in common. See 2026 per-sq-ft rates and full-home costs by builder tier, line by line.
keyTakeaways: Price on Carpet Area, Not Super Area — A super-area rate makes every quote look cheaper than it actually is per usable sq ft.
Builder Tier Changes Where the Money Goes — Across mid-segment, premium and luxury, full interiors land at roughly the same 10–15% of purchase price — just spent differently.
Mid-Segment Budgets Go to Storage — Kitchen and wardrobes take close to half the budget when the flat arrives with little built-in storage.
Luxury Budgets Pay a "Rework Premium" — Replacing a builder kitchen or re-routing AC ducting to personalise a show-flat finish rarely appears on a per-sq-ft quote.
Corridor-Specific Costs Add Up — Fit-out deposits, restricted work hours, lift booking and GST (about 18%) are routinely left off first budgets.
A 3BHK Runs ₹13–29L (Mid-Segment), ₹27–56L (Premium) or ₹60L+ (Luxury) — Before GST, based on 2026 corridor benchmarks by tier.
contentHtml:
In 2026, full-home interiors on Dwarka Expressway cost roughly ₹1,400–2,300 per sq ft of carpet area in mid-segment societies, ₹2,100–3,300 in premium societies, and ₹3,000–5,000+ in luxury and branded towers (before GST). That puts a typical 3BHK at about ₹13–29 lakh, ₹27–56 lakh or ₹60 lakh+ respectively. Builder tier matters because it decides what you inherit at handover and what you will have to replace.

Key takeaways

  • Price interiors on carpet area, not super area. A super-area rate makes every quote look cheaper than it is.
  • The builder tier changes where your money goes more than how much you spend as a share of the flat price. Across all three tiers, full interiors usually land at around 10–15% of the purchase price.
  • Mid-segment budgets go mostly into storage: kitchen and wardrobes. Luxury budgets go into loose furniture, lighting, and customising or reworking what the builder already installed.
  • Corridor-specific costs such as fit-out deposits, restricted work hours and lift booking add time and money. Ask your society for its fit-out rules before you sign a quote.

Why a single "cost per sq ft" doesn't work on Dwarka Expressway

Most interior cost guides give you one number for Gurgaon and move on. That number is not much use on Dwarka Expressway, because the corridor now holds very different products side by side. A mid-segment 3BHK in Sector 99 and a branded 4BHK in Sector 106 are both "Dwarka Expressway apartments", but the people buying them, the specification they get at handover and the interiors they want have almost nothing in common. For a city-wide view by BHK size instead of builder tier, see our interior design cost guide for Gurgaon.

The market itself has moved fast. Anarock's September 2026 report puts average residential prices on the corridor at about ₹14,180 per sq ft in H1 2026, up 135% since 2021 and now above the Gurugram average of ₹13,350. Square Yards counts around 115 active residential projects, from DLF, Signature Global, M3M, Smartworld, Elan, Godrej, Hero, Emaar, BPTP, Max Estates and others. Supply is weighted towards bigger homes: 3BHKs make up 39% and 4BHK+ another 28%.

So the useful question is not "what do interiors cost here?" but "what do interiors cost in a home like mine, from a builder like mine?" That is what this guide answers.

The three builder tiers on Dwarka Expressway

We group societies on the corridor into three tiers, based mainly on current price per sq ft and on what typically comes with the flat at possession. Individual towers vary, so treat the tier as a starting point and check your own possession specification sheet.

Rates exclude GST, appliances, art and décor. Property-rate bands are indicative 2026 market ranges, not quotes for any specific project.

What a 3BHK actually costs, line by line

Headline per-sq-ft rates hide where the money really goes. Here is how the budget typically splits for three representative homes we see often on the corridor: a 1,100 sq ft mid-segment 3BHK, a 1,500 sq ft premium 3BHK and a 2,800 sq ft luxury 4BHK.

Line item (₹ lakh)Mid-segment 3BHK (~1,100 sq ft)Premium 3BHK (~1,500 sq ft)Luxury 4BHK (~2,800 sq ft)

Two things stand out. In the mid-segment home, kitchen and wardrobes take close to half the budget, because the flat usually arrives with very little built-in storage. In the luxury home, loose furniture and lighting take the largest share, because the builder has already put in good flooring, bathroom fittings and often a kitchen. The work there is in making the home feel designed rather than delivered.

Tier by tier: what changes the number

Mid-segment societies: spend on storage, save on surfaces

In mid-segment towers, the handover is usually functional: vitrified tile flooring, a basic kitchen platform, standard bathroom fittings and no wardrobes. That makes the budget fairly predictable. Most of it goes into a modular kitchen and full-height wardrobes, with simple gypsum ceilings and good LED lighting doing the visual heavy lifting.

The trap here is over-spending on finishes that the layout can't carry. In compact 2BHK and 3BHK plans, a ₹2 lakh feature wall matters far less than a well-planned kitchen corner unit or a wardrobe with internal drawers. In our compact projects at Pareena Heights, the brief was much the same: open up a small living space and make every wall work for storage. See our modular kitchen layouts for Dwarka Expressway floor plans for how this plays out room by room.

Premium societies: the balanced budget

Premium societies hand over a better base, often with larger rooms, better windows and sometimes a partly fitted kitchen. The budget spreads more evenly across storage, lighting, wall treatments and furniture. This is also where costs vary the most, because the same 1,500 sq ft 3BHK can be done tastefully for ₹30 lakh or lavishly for ₹50 lakh.

A useful rule in this tier: decide early whether you are keeping what the builder installed. At Puri Emerald Bay, for example, we built a wood-finished modular kitchen with a centre island, which meant planning plumbing and electrical points around the island before any carpentry started. Late changes like that are where premium budgets quietly grow. Choosing between a 3BHK or 4BHK layout at this stage also shapes the budget considerably.

Luxury and branded towers: you are paying to personalise, and sometimes to undo

Luxury towers often come with imported marble or engineered wood floors, branded bathroom fittings, VRV air-conditioning and sometimes a fitted kitchen. That sounds like a saving, and partly it is. But owners at this level usually want the home to feel like theirs, not like a show flat, and that often means reworking finishes that are already there.

Removing and replacing a builder kitchen, re-routing AC ducting for a new ceiling design, or changing a marble pattern all carry a cost that rarely appears on a per-sq-ft quote. We call this the rework premium. In high-ceiling apartments it compounds: taller wardrobes, bigger curtain runs and more lighting points. In the open-plan Sobha apartment we delivered in Sector 108, much of the effort went into making a large living-dining space feel connected, rather than into adding more things.

The corridor-specific costs most quotes leave out

These are the costs that surprise homeowners on Dwarka Expressway, because they come from the society and the possession process rather than from the interior work itself.

  • Fit-out or interior deposit. Most societies ask for a refundable deposit before any work begins. The amount varies widely by society, so ask the facility management team in writing.
  • Restricted work hours. Noisy work is often limited to set weekday hours, with no work on Sundays. That stretches timelines, and longer timelines cost more in supervision.
  • Service lift booking and debris removal. Material movement needs lift slots, and debris has to leave the tower the same day. Budget for both.
  • Snagging and builder defects. New-possession flats on the corridor often have seepage, uneven walls or loose fittings. Get these fixed by the builder before interiors start, or you will pay twice.
  • GST. Interior work contracts generally attract GST, typically 18%. Always check whether a quote is inclusive or exclusive. On a ₹40 lakh project, that difference is about ₹7 lakh.

For the full list of extras that catch homeowners out, see our guide to hidden costs of interior design in Gurgaon.

A simple rule of thumb: 10–15% of your purchase price

Looking across the three tiers, one pattern holds up surprisingly well. Full interiors, including furniture, tend to land at about 10–15% of the price you paid for the flat. A ₹1.6 crore mid-segment 3BHK typically needs ₹15–25 lakh. A ₹3.5 crore premium 3BHK needs around ₹30–50 lakh. A ₹9–10 crore luxury 4BHK can easily need ₹90 lakh to ₹1.4 crore.

If your interior budget is well under 10% of the purchase price, plan to phase the work: do the kitchen, wardrobes, electrical and ceilings first, and add furniture and décor over time — our guide to no-cost EMI for interiors covers one way to spread that cost. If it is well over 15%, check whether you are paying for rework you don't really need.

How to get an accurate quote for your Dwarka Expressway apartment

  1. Share your carpet area and floor plan, not just the BHK count.
  2. Share the builder's possession specification sheet so the designer knows what you already have.
  3. Decide upfront what you are keeping, upgrading or replacing from the builder handover.
  4. Ask for an itemised quote with board grade, hardware brand and finish named for each line.
  5. Get the society's fit-out rules in writing and make sure the timeline reflects them.
  6. Confirm whether GST, design fees and site supervision are included.

For a deeper look at comparing quotes, see our guide on how to compare and negotiate interior design quotations.

faqs.question: How much does interior design cost on Dwarka Expressway in 2026?
faqs.answer: Full-home interiors cost about ₹1,400–2,300 per sq ft of carpet area in mid-segment societies, ₹2,100–3,300 in premium societies, and ₹3,000–5,000+ in luxury towers, before GST. A 3BHK typically costs ₹13–29 lakh, ₹27–56 lakh or ₹60 lakh+ depending on the tier.

faqs.question: Why do interiors cost more in luxury towers if the builder already provides marble and fittings?
faqs.answer: Because owners at this level usually personalise the home, which can mean replacing a builder kitchen, re-routing AC ducting or changing finishes. Larger rooms, higher ceilings and premium loose furniture also raise the total, even when flooring and bathroom fittings are already in place.

faqs.question: How much should I budget for interiors as a share of my flat price?
faqs.answer: A practical range is 10–15% of the purchase price for full interiors including furniture. Below 10%, plan to phase the work. Above 15%, check whether you are paying for rework you could avoid.

faqs.question: What is the interior cost of a 3BHK in a premium Dwarka Expressway society?
faqs.answer: For a 3BHK of about 1,300–1,700 sq ft carpet area in a premium society, expect roughly ₹27–56 lakh before GST, depending on materials, how much custom furniture you choose, and how much of the builder's handover you keep.

faqs.question: Should interior quotes be based on carpet area or super area?
faqs.answer: Carpet area. Super area includes walls, shafts and common areas you will never furnish. A rate quoted on super area looks lower but covers less real space, which makes quotes hard to compare.

faqs.question: Are there society charges before starting interior work?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Most Dwarka Expressway societies ask for a refundable fit-out deposit and set rules on work hours, lift use and debris removal. Get these in writing before finalising your timeline.

faqs.question: When should I start planning interiors for a new possession on Dwarka Expressway?
faqs.answer: Start design two to three months before possession, so drawings and material choices are ready by handover. Site work can then begin as soon as snagging is complete and the society approves the fit-out.
